source_or_privileged_boundary: A collaborator or synced-folder actor can rename unchanged content into and then out of a Tier-B-looking path while its content-addressed embedding task is permanently failed or has exhausted retries.
closest_control: Done tasks and retired_non_live tasks have dedicated exclusions, and task.rs defines permanent/finite retry policies, but hold_secret_embedding_tasks does not preserve or exclude terminal Failed state before overwriting it.
sink_or_broken_control: The dynamic secret-hold transition treats terminal failure state as replaceable classification metadata; unholding then feeds the task back to the online embedding send path despite the retry policy.
impact: Repeated third-party sends and charges for permanently invalid/exhausted work can consume per-adapter or device budget, keep indexing degraded, and bypass the operator-visible terminal state.

attack_path_facts.title: secret-hold cycles erase terminal embedding failure state
attack_steps: A lower-trust scope revision leaves an embedding task in a terminal or retry-exhausted Failed state.
The file name or classification changes to Tier B and a later index cycle demotes the failed task to a secrets_tier_b_hold state, overwriting its reason, attempts, and retry timing.
A subsequent non-secret revision is indexed and unhold converts the row to fresh Pending work with attempts reset to zero.
Normal enrichment reserves budget and invokes the configured embedding adapter again despite the original non-retryable or exhausted failure.
assumptions: A local content contributor can control names or revisions in a scope the operator continues to index.
An online embedding adapter was already approved and configured.
A terminal or retry-exhausted task exists before the secret/non-secret classification cycle.
attack_path_facts.context: KCS is a local CLI with no listener. The relevant boundary is destructive task-state reauthorization: lower-trust file revisions can combine with ordinary operator indexing to revive work that the retry contract made terminal.
attack_path_facts.exposure: Operator-mediated local filesystem workflow; the eventual adapter call is outbound only.
attack_path_facts.identity: The KCS OS user performs the call with the already configured adapter identity and budget authority; the lower-trust contributor controls file naming/revisions, not credentials or commands.
preconditions: A failed embedding task must already exist.
The same content must cycle into and out of Tier-B secret classification.
The operator must run the relevant index/enrichment cycles with online processing enabled.
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: plausible: an in-scope local content contributor can control the name and revision sequence, while operator invocations remain required
attack_path_facts.category: task lifecycle, retry-policy bypass, and bounded budget/network re-execution
mitigations: Done tasks and retired non-live tasks are excluded from hold demotion.
Adapter approval, tool, credential, and budget checks still apply to the revived send.
The issue does not grant a new destination or credential.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: local operator-mediated workflow with prior online-adapter authorization
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: task-state integrity, outbound adapter execution, and bounded cost
attack_path_facts.target_reach: one affected embedding task at a time within the indexed scope
secrets_references: The configured adapter credential may be used for the revived request, but the evidence shows no credential disclosure or destination change.
counterevidence: The reproduced sequence required content/name reclassification and repeated operator indexing.
Done and retired-non-live tasks do not enter the destructive transition.
Existing approval and budget controls bound the revived execution.
blindspots: The receipts do not establish how frequently attacker-controlled shared/synced revisions produce the full lifecycle.
Actual provider billing for the revived failure mode is adapter-dependent.
controls: Typed retry policy marks AuthError, InvalidInput, and ContractViolation non-retryable and caps NetworkError retries.
The hold selector excludes Done and retired non-live tasks, but not terminal or exhausted failures.
Pre-send approval and budget enforcement remain present.
attack_path_facts.rationale: The lower-trust file-revision path is realistic enough to avoid hard suppression, and the revived send/cost plus terminal-state loss is material but bounded. Medium impact with medium likelihood maps mechanically to Low/P3.
